primary.title: Dhammapada
primary.author: Gautama Buddha
primary.rationale: A collection of sayings and teachings attributed to Gautama Buddha, considered a foundational text in Buddhism. It is widely available in translation.

primary.title: Sutta Nipata
primary.author: Gautama Buddha
primary.rationale: An early collection of Buddhist scriptures, containing verses attributed to the Buddha. It is a significant source for understanding early Buddhist thought.

primary.title: Majjhima Nikaya
primary.author: Gautama Buddha
primary.rationale: A collection of the Buddha's middle-length discourses, offering insights into his teachings on various philosophical and ethical topics. It is a key text in the Pali Canon.

secondary.title: The Buddha and His Dhamma
secondary.author: B. R. Ambedkar
secondary.rationale: While published slightly before 1976, this work by a prominent scholar and social reformer offers a critical and modern interpretation of the Buddha's teachings and their social implications. It is highly influential.

secondary.title: What the Buddha Taught
secondary.author: Walpola Rahula
secondary.rationale: Another foundational text for understanding Buddhism, providing a clear and accessible explanation of the Buddha's core teachings. It is widely considered a standard introduction.

secondary.title: The Life of the Buddha: As Told by an English Follower
secondary.author: Arthur L. Herman
secondary.rationale: A scholarly biography that synthesizes historical and textual evidence to present a comprehensive account of the Buddha's life and teachings.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources attributed to Gautama Buddha are generally collections of his discourses and sayings, compiled by his disciples. Exact dating is approximate. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly merit and accessibility in understanding the figure and his teachings.
